surfaced_pitfalls.subject: Inconsistent capture byte budgets cap event-log size; jit claim acquire fails above 16 MiB
surfaced_pitfalls.detail: commands/claim.rs:191-194 sets CaptureBudget.max_bytes = 16 MiB on a CaptureSpec::phase_one that includes VirtualPath::EVENTS, so `jit claim acquire` errors ('captured 33519044 bytes but the maximum is 16777216') on the epic's own 10x benchmark fixture. commands/mod.rs:2186-2191 gives the issue-update path 64 MiB, which is why the label-update scenarios still run. No task in the breakdown names either constant. c88822a5 REQ-03 keeps the event log in the single-pass base specification and REQ-06 keeps capture budget-bounded, so the ceiling survives the retirement phase unless a task takes it. REFINED (wave 2): the whole-log PARSE (captured_events, mutation.rs:695, called only at :884 under MutationIntent::ClaimIssue) is claim-specific, so a label update never pays it and the benchmark medians stand. Two consequences split apart. (a) The claim ceiling is a real latent product bug -- `jit claim acquire` fails above 16 MiB -- but it is NOT on the path REQ-01/REQ-02 evidence measures. (b) The residual REQ-02 risk is different: the finalizer's whole-log copy (mutation.rs:1224, `.to_vec()` + compose_events) is addressed by b4483ad6 positioned-event-append, but capture still READS the log whole into the image, which c88822a5 REQ-03 explicitly preserves. A 33 MB read is roughly 10-15 ms against a ~100 ms budget, i.e. at or over REQ-02's 10 % margin, with no parse cost to remove.
surfaced_pitfalls.disposition: OPEN, split. (a) claim 16 MiB ceiling: create a remediation task inside the epic; it blocks no criterion but is an adjacent latent bug the epic surfaced. (b) REQ-02 margin from the whole-log read: this is the one that can fail a criterion. Decide at wave 16 (c88822a5) whether the single-pass base specification can take the log as length+tail rather than whole bytes, given the only whole-log consumer left is the claim path. Re-measure at wave 21 (722878d4) before accepting REQ-02.

surfaced_pitfalls.subject: The event-log capture ceiling survives in document.rs after 19e7298a closed it for claim and issue-update
surfaced_pitfalls.detail: DOCUMENT_CAPTURE_BUDGET (crates/jit/src/commands/document.rs:5-10) sets max_bytes = 64 MiB with max_listings: 0, and its capture specs declare VirtualPath::EVENTS (document.rs:295, :375, :957). So `jit doc add` fails on a repository whose event log exceeds 64 MiB -- the identical defect 19e7298a fixed for claim (16 MiB) and issue-update (64 MiB), at a higher threshold. The fix is now a one-liner of an established shape -- call issue_mutation_capture_budget() (commands/mod.rs:155) or apply the same u64::MAX + prose form that image.rs:594-604 and profile.rs record_capture_budget already establish. Raised to the user; folding it into this epic is a small task of the same class the user already directed be fixed now.

surfaced_pitfalls.subject: Six listing-expanding capture budgets declare the event log and keep a hand-picked byte ceiling
surfaced_pitfalls.detail: commands/gate.rs:251 (512 MiB, paths :296), commands/gate.rs:1110 (256 MiB, paths :1119), commands/gate_check.rs:783 (512 MiB, paths :790), commands/template.rs:35 (512 MiB, paths :388), commands/validate.rs:1256 MUTATION_CAPTURE_BUDGET (512 MiB, EVENTS discovered at validate.rs:411). All declare VirtualPath::EVENTS, so a large enough event log makes them fail the way claim did at 16 MiB and document at 64 MiB. They differ from those in one decisive respect: max_listings > 0, so max_bytes is the only bound on real capture growth there. Removing it deletes a live bound. commands/config.rs:304 and commands/init.rs:350 declare only VirtualPath::CONFIG and are confirmed unexposed.
surfaced_pitfalls.disposition: OPEN, and deliberately out of scope for 48e4f65c. The owner amended that issue's REQ-02 to budgets requesting no listings, matching its Background. Closing these needs a design for bounding listing expansion without a hand-picked byte number - the same problem image.rs:586-604 describes ('A budget here would restate that bound as a number this type cannot derive'). Exposure is low: the ceilings are 256-512 MiB. Not scheduled; surfaces in the completion report.

surfaced_pitfalls.subject: Epic REQ-02 is unreachable while the capture base specification reads the event log whole
surfaced_pitfalls.detail: Measured on a tmpfs copy via a throwaway examples binary driving the real RepositoryMutationSession::capture, 15 iterations x 3 passes: base capture is flat at 14.2/14.5 ms; adding VirtualPath::EVENTS costs 3.2 ms at 1x (3.37 MB) and 28.6 ms at 10x (33.7 MB). Slope 0.89 ms/MB. The hardware floor is 0.81 ms/MB (fs::read + Sha256::digest at ~2.4 GB/s on SHA-NI), i.e. 91% of measured - there is no implementation slack. REQ-02's budget is 0.34 ms/MB (10% of a projected 99.3 ms over 28.96 MB). One whole-log read is 2.6x over measured and 2.4x over the floor. Projection: 99.3 ms at 1x -> 125.0 ms at 10x = +26%, against REQ-02's required <10%.
surfaced_pitfalls.consumers: Eleven consumers of captured log bytes. Five need the whole log and NONE is on the label-update path (mutation.rs:695 claim reflection, archive.rs:465, migrate.rs:88, validation/repository.rs:428, memory.rs:502). The label-update path has four sites and no semantic consumer: composer prefix copy (mutation.rs:1225, deleted by b4483ad6), torn-tail inspection (:1230, last line only), expected preimage (:1273, whole-log SHA-256), apply-time read-set re-capture (repository_state_store.rs:535). The last two are conflict machinery that ensure_write_set_unchanged already answers with length + 4 KiB tail.
false_premises_in_c88822a5: 'The apply-time round is already gone' - it is not; repository_state_store.rs:526-538 still re-captures the whole read set and compares it whole, a third whole-log read per changing label update.
ensure_write_set_unchanged (faa668c9) has no production caller, only repository_state_store_tests.rs:5108 - correct for the phase, but c88822a5's premise assumes it is live.
surfaced_pitfalls.disposition: RESOLVED by the invoker (session 2, ESC-05): option A. c88822a5 REQ-03 is amended to read the event log as length and a bounded tail, with a command that parses the log naming it whole in its own capture set. Epic REQ-02 stands unchanged; projected difference falls under 1 %. The amendment's three implied consequences are stated in c88822a5's Notes so they are delivered by that issue rather than falling between issues: a per-path read mode in CaptureSpec, a captured entry carrying length+tail (EventLogTail made reachable), and expected_of no longer deriving the log's preimage from a whole-log digest. The spike is linked to c88822a5 as its evidence. Re-measure at 722878d4 (wave 21) before accepting REQ-02.

process_findings.finding: The planning bracket's planning node carries only plan-review. Documentation commits under it changed AGENTS.md and packaged gate content, both asserted by the Rust suite, with no Rust gate in their path. main went red for three commits undetected.
process_findings.suggested_remedy: Consider a cargo-ci gate on the planning node in .jit/templates.toml. NOT actioned: the template is shipped-profile content and a gate change is a scope change requiring owner approval.

process_findings.finding: Evaluating a cargo-ci gate on main while a worker runs its own cargo-ci in a worktree oversubscribes the machine (load avg 8+). Observed twice on 555ff4be: run 1 hit LD-7's 20s per-test bound with 6 dogfood-fixture timeouts plus a 42s suite-duration budget failure; run 2 exceeded the gate's own 900s checker timeout and recorded exit=None with empty stdout.
process_findings.suggested_remedy: Serialize gate evaluation against worker builds: wait for every dispatched worker in the wave to go idle before evaluating any cargo-ci gate. The 4-worker parallelism cap governs dispatch, not CPU-bound gate runs.
process_findings.status: adopted by the lead for the rest of this epic

process_findings.finding: The shared cache pool served a corrupt seed. Worker faa668c9 found the pre-seeded target/ unusable: serde rlib/rmeta could not be loaded by rustc 1.97.0 (E0463) while main's identically named artifacts loaded fine; cargo clean plus a 68s rebuild fixed it. Mechanism: reclaim-worker-worktree.sh harvests every git-ignored top-level directory back into one pool 'newest file wins' (documented in worktree-dispatch-protocol.md). After wave 1 the lead reclaimed TWO independently built worktrees into the same pool, so the pool became a file-by-file merge of two build trees that were never internally consistent. dispatch-worker-worktree.sh then seeds each new worktree with `cp -al` (hardlinks), propagating that inconsistent set.
process_findings.suggested_remedy: Script-level: harvest should be per-wave-exclusive or fingerprint-keyed rather than newest-file-wins across build trees. NOT actioned -- the scripts are shared cross-project infrastructure (canonical copy lives with the skill) and changing one is escalation category 8.
process_findings.lead_action: Deleted .agents/cache-pool (23 GB) per the protocol's own remedy: 'delete it and let the next harvest rebuild it warm -- it is a cache, never a source of truth'. Adopted for the rest of this epic: harvest at most ONE worktree per wave into the pool; remove the remaining worktrees without harvesting, so two build trees are never merged.
process_findings.status: mitigated by the lead; script design raised to the user, not changed

process_findings.finding: A backgrounded gate evaluation reported 'completed (exit code 0)' while the gate itself FAILED. The notification carried the exit status of the shell pipeline (`jit gate evaluate ... | tail -3`), not of the gate. Acting on that summary would have completed an issue whose code-review found a blocking corruption path.
process_findings.suggested_remedy: Never read a backgrounded gate's outcome from the task-notification exit code. Read the gate-run record, or re-query `jit issue show <id> --json` gate statuses, before drawing any conclusion.

process_findings.finding: A gate result recorded as `passed` does not say which tree it judged. `jit issue show --json` and `jit gate status-all` report gates[].status with last_run_at and nothing relating that run to HEAD. 35544121's code-review read `passed` from an 11:14Z run while the module it reviewed had since been rewritten (130 lines in the exact file its only finding pointed at). Accepting that readout would have completed the issue on a review of code that no longer existed.
process_findings.suggested_remedy: Surface staleness where readiness is read. The gate-run record already carries the evidence — its stdout opens with an `Attribution:` commit list — so a `stale` flag when HEAD has moved past the attributed commits would turn a judgement call into a fact. NOT actioned: this is a shipped surface, escalation category 8.
process_findings.lead_action: Adopted for the rest of this epic: after every merge, re-evaluate every AI-review gate on the issue before reading its status, and confirm the run's Attribution line covers the new commits.
process_findings.status: adopted by the lead; product change raised to the user, not actioned

process_findings.finding: The lead's dispatch prompt for 4e818d10 instructed the worker to delete the memory kernel modelling, citing the issue's Notes line 'against roughly 340 lines of kernel modelling this replaces' and @/inv/canonical-cutover. Both were misread: the Notes line frames the EPIC's net line balance, and LD-11 is itself the named versioned boundary @/inv/canonical-cutover asks for, naming b0ee2dd6 as the removal condition. Following the instruction would have broken 21e976d1 REQ-03. The worker refused, stated its evidence, and proceeded additively without blocking.
process_findings.suggested_remedy: Before composing a dispatch prompt, read the parent story's criteria and grep the plan's decision table for the task's subject. The lead had read 21e976d1 REQ-03 earlier in the same session and still composed a prompt contradicting it.
process_findings.lead_action: Corrected the instruction to the worker in writing, with the evidence, and recorded the error here.

process_findings.finding: An inherited lint allowance propagates when a worker extends an existing export statement rather than adding its own. The worker placed MemoryRedoApplier inside the allow-ed `pub use memory::{...}` line, which put a brand-new type under a suppression that story 21e976d1 REQ-04 forbids in spirit (`through declared visibility rather than a dead-code allowance`). The worker's report called it 'no dead-code allowance', literally true of the lint name and misleading about what a reviewer sees.
process_findings.suggested_remedy: When reviewing a diff that adds a public item, check the visibility statement it joins, not just the item. The one-minute experiment (split the export, run clippy -D warnings on the worker's warm build) settled it without a review round and cost the lead nothing.
process_findings.status: resolved in-wave at 0612382b4; technique adopted by the lead

process_findings.finding: rustc masks a struct-literal privacy error behind a later field-access error. When a test both constructs a type by struct literal AND later reads one of its fields, making the fields private surfaces only the E0616 field-access error; the E0451 construction error is dropped. The 8559f529 worker reproduced this in an isolated ten-line crate rather than asserting it.
process_findings.why_it_matters: Fixing only the errors cargo reports, then building clean, does NOT prove that no bypassing construction site remains. The build is not the proof. A textual grep for the struct-literal form is.
process_findings.lead_action: Adopted: when a change's purpose is to make a construction path unreachable, the evidence is a grep over the construction form, not a green build. Applied here — grep confirmed `RedoRecord {` survives only inside redo_record.rs's own test submodule.
process_findings.status: adopted by the lead; credited to the 8559f529 worker

process_findings.finding: A naive production-line count is wrong in two directions at once. Cutting each file at its first #[cfg(test)] counted redo_conformance.rs's 447 test lines as production (the file is gated by #[cfg(test)] mod on its DECLARATION in mod.rs, not inside the file) and truncated memory.rs at line 146, where two #[cfg(test)] function attributes sit above 200-odd production lines. It reported 1428 where the correct figure is 1137. Cumulative additions across a task's commits measure churn, not footprint: 35544121 added 413 and removed 93 of its own across three rounds, delivering 320.
process_findings.lead_action: Measure by brace-matching each #[cfg(test)] item's extent, excluding cfg(test)-declared modules whole, and report net per task attributed by the jit: commit tag. Method written into footprint.md so 722878d4 (wave 21, ER-01) reuses it rather than re-deriving it.

process_findings.finding: Evidence offered for a criterion must be reproducible, not asserted. The lead wrote a measurement method into prose and quoted figures from an ad-hoc script it never committed. holistic-review rejected the figures as self-attested.
process_findings.lead_action: Commit the generator alongside any measurement an issue's criteria rest on, quote its verbatim output, and make it parameterised for the later consumer. Applies directly to ER-01 at wave 21 and to epic REQ-01/REQ-02's benchmark evidence, where bench.sh already sets the right precedent.

process_findings.finding: A worker's cargo-ci run costs ~8 minutes where a no-change run on main costs 26 s and a docs-change run 100 s. Measured breakdown of the 100 s run: clippy 30 s, suite-build 40 s (17 executables, 2.09 GB linked), test 22.7 s over 4732 tests, doctest 4.5 s. The cause is crate granularity, not gate configuration: crates/jit is one compilation unit of 198,814 src lines (190,515 outside test-named files) with 37 direct dependencies, and the workspace has two members. Rust recompiles per crate, so an edit anywhere under storage/ re-type-checks and re-codegens the whole crate, twice per run (clippy's --all-targets check pass, then the test build), before 17 binaries relink. CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 is banned in force by the bounded-rust-build-footprint budget, so no incremental reuse offsets it. scripts/cargo-ci.sh additionally takes a host-wide flock by design, so a four-worker wave queues four such runs.
process_findings.lead_action: Out of this epic's scope; recorded for v1.0 triage rather than acted on. Within scope, the lead refreshes the cache pool from main's target directory at each wave boundary instead of harvesting one worker's worktree: main is exactly the commit the next wave anchors to and its warm tree is 60 GB against the pool's 23 GB, so the seeded worktrees stop re-paying the unchanged base. The structural fix is splitting crates/jit along the layer boundaries AGENTS.md already mandates (domain+graph pure, storage, commands, cli/output), which would make a storage edit stop rebuilding main.rs and commands/profile.rs; it is a large refactor that would collide with this epic's in-flight work and belongs after it. Re-enabling incremental for worker runs while keeping the CI ban is a cheaper stopgap but changes an enforced invariant's budget, so it needs the invoker (escalation category 8). sccache is running at a 6.45 % hit rate and is contributing nothing; same category.
process_findings.status: recorded, not acted on; surfaced to the invoker

process_findings.finding: PF-11's headline number was misattributed. The cargo-ci gate costs 78 s warm and 128 s cold on an idle host, measured on isolated target directories. The '~8 minutes per worker run' is the host-wide flock in scripts/cargo-ci.sh serializing a four-worker wave -- queue time, not compile time. PF-11's structural claim (crates/jit is one 197k-line compilation unit) stands; its cost attribution did not.
process_findings.lead_action: Re-measured before acting. Three candidate interventions were measured and rejected: lld (inert -- rust-lld is already the default linker on x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, confirmed by `readelf -p .comment`); raising the flock to 2 slots (88 s against 110 s serial, and BOTH runs failed the suite-duration budget at 38.3/33.3 s against 30 s, because that budget is defined over an idle host); tmpfs worker targets (storage medium is not the bottleneck -- SATA 79 s against NVMe 78 s -- and MemAvailable never fell below 48.06 GB of 62).
process_findings.status: measured; POL-03 applied, the other three rejected with evidence

process_findings.finding: sccache is neither broken nor useless: its Rust cache key is bound to the absolute target-directory path, because Cargo passes absolute --extern and -L paths on the rustc command line. Two cold builds at the SAME CARGO_TARGET_DIR: pass 1 37 s with 244 Rust misses and 0 hits, pass 2 7 s with 244 Rust hits (100 %). Across different paths it is 0.00 % in every configuration tested, including CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0. Every agent worktree has its own target path, so sccache misses 100 % of the time in the only scenario it was installed for, costing ~3 s per cold build (68 s with, 65 s without) and 73 GB of disk.
process_findings.why_it_matters: The cache pool in dispatch-worker-worktree.sh already does this job strictly better -- it hardlinks a warm target/ into each worktree, so the worker skips compilation rather than replaying it at 7 s. sccache is redundant when the pool is healthy and useless when it is not. Making it pay would need one shared target-dir path, which jit:be005f64 already rejected because Cargo's single target-dir lock would serialize every concurrent agent build.
process_findings.lead_action: Recorded, not acted on: removing RUSTC_WRAPPER from scripts/cargo-ci.sh is a shared-infrastructure change (escalation category 8) and saves ~3 s. Raised to the user. Keeping the cache pool healthy -- and moving it off the 84 %-full SATA root onto /data (NVMe, 301 GB free) via LEAD_CACHE_POOL -- is the higher-value follow-up.
process_findings.corrections: Two mechanisms were asserted before this one was measured, and both were wrong: (a) that RUSTC_WRAPPER split Cargo fingerprints between gate and interactive builds -- checked, not supported, all libc fingerprints carried an identical rustc hash; (b) that incremental compilation poisoned the sccache key -- refuted, CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 still gave 0.00 % Rust hits.
process_findings.status: recorded, not acted on; surfaced to the user

process_findings.finding: `jit gate evaluate` memoizes an automated gate's verdict over unchanged declared inputs: a re-run reports `Duration: 0ms` and `Verdict: taken from run <id> over the same declared inputs`, reusing the prior FAIL. The standing remedy for LD-7 -- 're-run once warm' -- therefore does nothing without `--force`.
process_findings.suggested_remedy: Use `jit gate evaluate <id> <gate> --force` for every warm re-run of a timing failure. Adopted by the lead for the rest of this epic.

process_findings.finding: A gate run's `Tree: dirty` line can report only the tracker's own records. `jit claim acquire` appends to .jit/events.jsonl and rewrites the issue file before the checker starts, so a gate evaluated straight after a clean merge reports dirty with no source change in the tree.
process_findings.suggested_remedy: Commit tracker state after each claim/evaluate pair before reading a `Tree:` line as a statement about the source tree; `git status --porcelain` separates the two.

process_findings.finding: A worker's completion report does not mean its processes have exited, and a lead message sent to a reported-done worker puts it back to work. The lead sent w-0938d99e an added @/inv/essential-code-prose constraint just as it reported; the worker resumed and started rebuilding in its worktree while the lead merged the branch and evaluated cargo-ci on main. The two builds collided: suite-clock 97493 ms and suite-build 54114 ms against a 22.4 s / 0.6 s warm baseline, load average 10.3, with the worker's own rust-lld and rustc processes visible in its worktree target. The gate's FAIL said nothing about the tree.
process_findings.suggested_remedy: Confirm a worker is IDLE (ListAgents, not its report) before merging or gating its branch. Deliver any added constraint before dispatch, not after a report; when one must be sent late, expect the worker to resume and do not start a gate until it goes idle again.

evidence_requirements.requirement: Report the REQ-06 line balance ATTRIBUTED, not just as one number. Report (a) the literal cumulative total LD-6 names -- `git diff --shortstat 34d37f8be -- '*.rs'` -- which is what REQ-06 is judged on, and (b) the redo-record-only subtotal, excluding in-epic remediation work that is not redo-record work.

Three in-epic tasks are not redo-record work: ce053478 (net +18, done), the claim-ceiling task, and the prose-checks task (projected ~-390 from deleting code_review_policy_test.rs and the packaged-citation test). If the redo-record work alone were net positive, that -390 would flip the total negative and REQ-06 would read green while the epic's premise -- that the storage layer ends smaller -- stayed unproven.
excluded_from_subtotal: 1fce64b78 (POL-03 build-time commit, session 4, -139 Rust lines; carries no jit issue by POL-03's terms)
evidence_requirements.note: This does NOT soften REQ-06. The criterion is judged on its literal cumulative total. The subtotal is supplementary so a reviewer can see the mechanism claim independently. Session 4 added the POL-03 commit to the exclusion list: it is build-tooling work, carries no jit issue, and removes 139 Rust lines that would otherwise flatter REQ-06's literal total. 8559f529 is NOT excluded.

verifications.what: code-review round 1 found a security-relevant corruption path the lead's own review missed.
verifications.detail: redo_apply.rs:167 staged puts with cap-std `Dir::create` at a predictable `.{leaf}.{pid}.redo.tmp` name. That call is create+truncate and follows symlinks, so a pre-existing in-root symlink at the stage name truncates an unrelated file, receives the put bytes, and is then renamed onto the put target - the record writes a path it never named. References @/charter/D-17 and @/invariant/atomic-writes.
verifications.lead_note: The lead verified phasing, the interruption contract, line budget and caller absence, but did not inspect the staging open. Second defect in this epic caught by @/inv/atomic-writes; the first was the truncating record write in 555ff4be. Both were in new-file publication paths.

verifications.what: BLOCKING: code-review round 1's finding is unaddressed at HEAD and round 3 passed without re-checking it.
verifications.detail: R1 (blocking, issue-impact, redo_apply.rs:85): 'REQ-05 requires a backend-held interruption injector, but apply_record receives one per call and no backend owns it. Callers can therefore vary injection across applications rather than the backend owning its interruption boundary.' At HEAD apply_record still takes `injector: &dyn RedoInterruptionInjector` (redo_apply.rs:88) and no backend holds it. R2 flagged the staging vulnerability instead; the lead dispatched rework for R2 only. R3 passed with 'All hard criteria are implemented and the prior staging vulnerability is remediated' - it re-checked the staging finding and not R1.
verifications.lead_note: Caught by the Tier 1.5 prior-findings regression check, which exists precisely because reviewers have no memory across rounds. The issue is NOT completed. The worker's original position was that the session becomes the injector holder at wiring time (4319256e), matching the kernel's `execute_repository_delta(..., &*self.injector)` pattern - arguable, but No-argue discipline forbids the lead softening REQ-05 by argument. Resolve by changing the artifact or by escalating.
verifications.verdict: FAIL confirmed at HEAD in session 2 (apply_record still took the injector per call at redo_apply.rs:88). RESOLVED by the invoker (ESC-06): change the artifact — redo_apply.rs gains a type holding Arc<dyn RedoInterruptionInjector> with apply(&self, roots, record), mirroring FileTransactionKernel (file_transaction.rs:69). The free-function form does not survive beside it (@/inv/canonical-cutover). Rework attempt 3 dispatched; the invoker's guidance reset the counter.

verifications.what: Held-injector rework accepted; a new blocking durability finding replaced it.
verifications.detail: The invoker-approved RedoApplier shape landed and was merged to main at 94fb377b7. R1 (injector held) and R2 (staging create_new + no-follow) both verified closed at HEAD. cargo-ci passed on the MERGED tree (4709 tests, zero warnings). Re-evaluating code-review against the new commits produced R4, a new finding: put_file calls root.create_dir_all(directories) at redo_apply.rs:171 and then syncs only the deepest directory, so for a put at a/b/c/file the entries for c in b, b in a, and a in the root are never fsynced. remove_record then runs, and a crash loses the nested put with no record left to replay. References @/charter/D-17 and @/inv/derived-state-coherence.
verifications.lead_note: Lead-verified at HEAD before dispatching. This is the THIRD defect in this epic found in a new-file publication path, after 555ff4be's truncating record write and 35544121's symlink-following stage open. All three were durability or containment properties of publishing a file that did not exist before. Worth naming in the 21e976d1 checkpoint review as a pattern rather than three unrelated bugs.
verifications.verdict: RESOLVED. open_or_create_capability_parent (repository_state_store.rs:1636) creates and syncs one level at a time inside the NotFound arm only, so a/b/c syncs root, a and b before the walk descends, and put_file's existing sync covers c. An existing ancestor costs no fsync. A symlinked ancestor still takes the Ok arm and is refused by open_child_dir_nofollow. cargo-ci passed on the merged tree (4710 tests); code-review passed with 0 findings, attribution covering fc698cfe3/2920ded44/c72c700c7.

verifications.what: The fsync ordering the R4 fix establishes has no owning test; only the crash-window ordering does.
verifications.detail: test_redo_applier_apply_keeps_the_record_until_a_fresh_nested_put_is_published (redo_apply.rs:475) owns the property that the record outlives a fresh nested put's publication, and it was GREEN BEFORE the fix — the worker disclosed this rather than letting it pass as evidence. The sync itself has no failure seam at this layer: sync_capability_directory operates on an already-open handle via try_clone + sync_all, so the 0o300 no-read-permission trick that makes redo_record's path-based sync_directory observable does not apply here. Adding a RedoPoint for directory creation would widen the point enum that 4e818d10 REQ-04 and d591a1c8 REQ-01 require both backends to share, and the in-memory backend has no directories, so that seam would be wrong.
verifications.lead_note: Accepted, not waived. @/inv/orthogonal-tests requires an owning test at the cheapest layer THAT CAN OBSERVE the property; no layer here observes it cheaply. The ordering is structural — the sync sits inside the create arm before the walk descends — and was verified by reading, by the code-review gate that raised the finding, and by the gate's explicit recheck. Precedent: open_capability_parent likewise has no owning test and is proven through its consumers. Carried to the 21e976d1 checkpoint (wave 6) so holistic-review sees it rather than discovering it.

verifications.what: Cross-backend divergence on a constructible record; lead-verified claims that did hold.
verifications.detail: code-review F1 (blocking): a record putting issues/a.json then issues makes the memory put_entry overwrite the Directory entry with a File while keeping its child, where the filesystem applier fails on the nonempty-directory replacement and leaves its record. Memory reports success and clears the residue (memory.rs:608-610). 835bae3f REQ-02 rejects paths outside the roots at construction but nothing rejects an ancestor/descendant pair, so the record is constructible. F2 (advisory): MemoryRedoApplier::new rustdoc restates its one-field initializer (@/inv/essential-code-prose).
verifications.lead_evidence: Verified before dispatching rework: memory_file_object(path) is format!("memory-file:{path:?}"), byte-identical to the inline form it replaced, so the kernel's entries are unchanged; and repository_state_store.rs never names MemoryRepositoryState.record — its only RedoRecord reference is faa668c9's ensure_write_set_unchanged, still with no production caller. So the worker's reachability audit holds and 21e976d1 REQ-03 is satisfied for this issue's work.
verifications.verdict: RESOLVED. The worker measured RedoApplier's actual contract with three throwaway probes rather than assuming it, and matched all four rows: EISDIR for a put over a directory an earlier put created, UnsafeTarget(component) for the mirror order and for a non-directory ancestor, EISDIR for a delete of a directory. No rollback in any case — earlier operations stand and the record stays installed, which redo-only convergence requires. Two self-corrections fell out: memory walks ancestors outermost-first so UnsafeTarget names the same component, and the worker's earlier Unaddressable claim for a non-directory ancestor was the wrong error shape. F2's rustdoc deleted. Both gates green on the merged tree; code-review attribution covers 2c0d5d63b and 667460a66.

verifications.what: The overlap check was implemented as an optional constructor beside pub fields.
verifications.detail: RedoRecord::new validates and parse calls the same helper, but redo_record.rs:56-58 leaves puts, deletes and event_append pub, so `RedoRecord { puts: vec![put(issues/a.json), put(issues)], ..Default::default() }` still constructs the overlapping record the task exists to prevent. REQ-01 says 'rejected at construction'; a struct literal is construction. Compounding it, the struct rustdoc at :49-53 now states 'Operation paths are pairwise disjoint ... checked identically at construction and at parse' as fact, so the type documents an invariant it permits callers to violate.
verifications.lead_note: Caught at Tier 2 from the worker's own disclosure — it reported 'Fields stay pub ... existing struct-literal test fixtures were out of scope'. The asymmetry that makes it wrong: 835bae3f's root-class rejection lives in VirtualPath's constructor and CANNOT be bypassed, because no path reaches RedoRecord without passing it. The worker matched that check's placement without matching its unbypassability. PARTLY THE LEAD'S FAULT: the issue Notes said 'roughly 30 production lines', costing the comparison logic and not the encapsulation that makes it binding, and the worker sized to that number. The estimate is descriptive and does not override a criterion; not amended.
verifications.verdict: FAIL - rework 1 of 2. Fields become private with read accessors; 43 struct-literal sites across four files (all tests) route through new(); the shared arbitrary_record() generator must produce disjoint sets by construction rather than prop_assume filtering, since d591a1c8 builds its conformance suite on that fixture next.

verifications.what: The encapsulation rework silently dropped the no-rollback property owned by a completed issue's test.
verifications.detail: Making RedoRecord's overlap check unbypassable made two memory.rs records unconstructible, so the worker redesigned their tests — correct in principle and clearly disclosed. But test_memory_redo_applier_apply_refuses_a_put_over_a_directory_an_earlier_put_created owned an assertion its replacement does not carry: 'the refusal undid a put that had already landed'. That is the no-rollback property — a refusal leaves the record's EARLIER operations applied — which 4e818d10's worker established by measurement and which epic REQ-03 rests on. Both replacements apply single-put records, so no earlier operation exists to preserve; the delete test is single-operation too. A backend that rolled back on refusal would pass every test in the tree.
verifications.lead_evidence: Found by diffing the test inventory of both backends between main and the branch (two memory.rs names replaced by one, redo_apply.rs unchanged), then reading the deleted bodies assertion by assertion. Grepping both backends for the assertion's substance returns nothing. Not covered on the filesystem side either, and correctly so: 4e818d10's worker established that half with throwaway probes because the behaviour belongs to 35544121 under @/inv/orthogonal-tests.
verifications.lead_note: The property is still expressible under the new validation — two puts that do not contain one another, e.g. index.json and issues, against a pre-existing directory at issues. The obligation to restore it falls on the change that removed the owner, not on the closed issue.
verifications.verdict: RESOLVED. test_memory_redo_applier_apply_leaves_an_earlier_put_applied_after_a_later_one_is_refused restores it with a disjoint two-put record (index.json then issues, against an independently seeded directory): the first put's bytes stand, the second refuses IsADirectory, the record stays installed. The worker's audit for a SECOND lost property is the notable part and the lead verified it: the deleted mirror test also asserted no-rollback, but at the ancestor-walk guard. The worker wrote that test, watched it fail, and traced the cause rather than adjusting it to pass — apply resolves every operation's path in one batch before BeforeApply (memory.rs:578-585, mirroring redo_apply.rs), so a pre-existing bad ancestor refuses the whole record before anything lands. The only way that guard ever fired mid-pass required two operations naming one path as the other's ancestor, which this issue makes unconstructible. So the scenario is retired by the fix, not lost by redesign, and the upfront-refusal property it leaves behind is already owned by the untouched test_memory_redo_applier_apply_refuses_a_data_path_while_the_data_root_is_absent.

verifications.what: REQ-02's pre-durability property is implied by the suite but owned by no test.
verifications.detail: code-review F1 (blocking): committed() writes the record before every tested application (redo_conformance.rs:205), and the first injectable RedoPoint follows that commit, so no test interrupts before the record is durable. REQ-02 reads 'After an interruption before the record is durable, the repository reads back as the complete old state.'
verifications.lead_evidence: Verified before relaying. nothing_published does assert commit publishes nothing (:251-255), and that plus 'the first live write follows BeforeApply' IMPLIES the property — but an implication drawn from two other assertions is not the owning test the criterion asks for. The structural cause: RedoInterruptionInjector is consulted only inside apply, while durability happens in RedoRecord::commit / commit_record, which has no seam. No RedoPoint value lies in the pre-durability window, so reclassifying points cannot reach it.
verifications.lead_note: Told the worker NOT to widen RedoPoint: it is 35544121's closed enum over the apply pass, and 4e818d10 REQ-04 requires both backends to step the same values while their commits differ. If the worker concludes REQ-02 is unreachable without widening it, that returns to the lead as an escalation. Likely honest shape: a torn or absent record leaves the complete old state, observable without touching any enum. Session-open replay stays with 0938d99e (wave 9) per this issue's own Notes.
verifications.verdict: RESOLVED. prop_an_interruption_during_the_records_commit_leaves_the_complete_old_state runs the real commit, cuts its output back to every proper prefix of the bytes written, and asserts the repository reads complete-old at each. RedoPoint untouched: the worker confirmed widening it could not have helped, since no injector call exists in the commit path to carry a new variant. Filesystem backend alone, with the reason in the test — InMemoryStorage::commit_record is a single assignment (memory.rs:536-545, lead-verified) so its pre-durability window has no interior. The completed-commit instant stays covered on both backends by prop_nothing_is_published_before_the_pass_reaches_its_first_live_write; proper prefixes and the complete commit are different instants, so the two do not overlap.

verifications.what: The worker's `test-support` manifest prose against the visibility it describes.
verifications.detail: Commit 8828f6814 rewrote crates/jit/Cargo.toml's test-support comment to say the feature exposes 'mutation interruption points/injectors ... as part of the crate's public API' and that it 'only widens their visibility from pub(crate) to pub', so 'cargo build and release builds drop the surface'. False for the two items named: storage/mod.rs re-exports MutationPoint and MutationInterruptionInjector with an unconditional `pub use`, so a default build keeps them. crates/server/Cargo.toml carried the same error in its parenthetical example.
verifications.resolution: Lead corrected the prose rather than gating the exports (22dd9455f).
